clue.text: Needs rice for home use

indicators.note: the letters of the first two words are put to a different use, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone needs rice for their own kitchen at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'use' is the anagram signal: NEEDS RICE is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A residence is a dwelling place, the house where someone lives.

clue.text: The team is even cut by the French

indicators.note: the word even is split open by another piece, which goes inside it

parts.note: taken as written
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: A sports side is evenly matched until the French interfere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The team' reads as the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition: a side of that many players.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has this many players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Actually one quarter act

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
N, north, is one quarter of the compass
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone claims a single quarter of a play really happened.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points are the 'quarters' in crosswords: N, S, E or W.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are emphatic adverbs meaning in truth or in fact.

clue.text: Remove the tax

definitions.meaning: to cut out, as a surgeon cuts out tissue
a duty charged on goods made at home, such as alcohol

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means cut away; as a noun it is a duty levied on home-produced goods.

clue.text: Study only comfort

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
sole means only, as in sole survivor

explanation.surface: Reading is someone's only solace.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to give them comfort in grief.

clue.text: Support a form of transport that's inferior

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Backing a mode of transport that is second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of second rank or lesser importance is lower in standing.

clue.text: Making bloomers, ruin games

indicators.note: the letters of the next words are used to make something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Blunders, someone claims, spoil the fun of games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' looks like blunders or knickers, but here it means flowers, things that bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: These are popular garden flowering plants, so they are literally things that bloom.

clue.text: Check on fellow cleaner

parts.note: to deter is to check or hold back
a gent is a man or fellow

explanation.surface: A supervisor checks up on a colleague who cleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets one piece after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing powder or liquid is a cleaning agent.

clue.text: Strike out as allowed in the river

indicators.note: the word for allowed is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales and England
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A permitted strike happens by the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete text is to cross it out.

clue.text: Poor beggar! He's unable to better himself

parts.note: to mend something is to improve or better it
what a man unable to do something would say: I can't

explanation.surface: Pity the poor man who can never improve his lot in life.
explanation.walkthrough: The beggar's words 'mend I can't' run together to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mendicant lives by asking for alms, so he is a poor man who begs.

clue.text: Feel over-sentimental about the silver in senility

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to dote on someone is to be foolishly fond of them
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An old person grows sentimental over their silver wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the silver' looks like an anniversary or heirloom, but it is the chemical symbol, which sits inside the verb for being foolishly fond.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age with its loss of mental sharpness is a synonym of senility.

clue.text: Touching account of a falling back

parts.note: re means touching on, concerning
a version is one person's account of events

explanation.surface: A moving story of somebody's relapse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reversion is a return to an earlier state, a relapse.

clue.text: Putting on a minister in the German capital

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, a degree held by many ministers

indicators.note: the capital letter of a word is its first

explanation.surface: A clergyman is visiting Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the German capital' is not Berlin but the first letter of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something on means adding it to what is there.

clue.text: Showing ill-humour, scoffed when sober

parts.note: temper means a bad mood
to scoff is to eat greedily, so scoffed means ate

explanation.surface: A grumpy person eats a great deal but stays sober.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moderate in drink is abstemious, sober.

clue.text: Rule a girl out of order, though it's irregular

indicators.note: the letters are not in their proper order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A regulation forbidding a girl's behaviour is deemed irregular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular' is a noun here: an irregular soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter in an unofficial armed band, not a regular soldier.

clue.text: Being furious about subordinate, egg-head made complaint

indicators.note: the word for furious goes around the other pieces

parts.note: mad means very angry
under means lower in rank

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A furious boss complains about his junior, an intellectual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg-head' looks like an intellectual but gives only the first letter of egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To maunder is to grumble or ramble on, so made complaint is fair.

clue.text: Hard to place

definitions.meaning: concrete or jelly that has become firm
to put something down in position

explanation.definitionFit: Firm or solidified; and as a verb, to put something somewhere.

clue.text: Taking a bit of cheese and a roll at lunchtime in the main

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Someone has some cheese and a bread roll for lunch out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old poetic word for the open ocean.

clue.text: Drink for a youngster?

explanation.definitionFit: A small dram of whisky; and a toddler, a little child.

clue.text: Bearing with a Greek character slow to follow

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
late means behind time, slow

explanation.surface: With a Greek hero's slow bearing, someone trails behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate is to copy or imitate someone, following their example.

clue.text: Sporting people smear on make-up

indicators.note: the letters are made up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Athletes put on cosmetics before a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics but signals the anagram of SMEAR ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers are sportsmen who propel boats with oars.

clue.text: Expertise in a particular trade

indicators.note: the letters lie within the next two words, straddling them

explanation.surface: Someone has a knack for one craft.
explanation.definitionFit: Art means skill or craft, as in the art of conversation.

clue.text: Goes after some soldiers, but comes back

indicators.note: the word for goes is placed after the soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
turns, as in goes or takes turns in a game

explanation.surface: A man pursues a group of troops, then retreats.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns means goes back or comes back again.

clue.text: Family man maybe making a periodical payment on the quiet

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed on, that is after, the quiet one

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
rent is paid each month or week

explanation.surface: A father pays the rent without telling anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets A and RENT after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A father is one kind of family parent, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: A club graduates hasten to join

parts.note: MAs, holders of Masters of Arts degrees
hie is an old word for hurry

explanation.surface: A society that graduates rush to join.
explanation.walkthrough: A mashie is an old golf club, roughly a five-iron.
explanation.definitionFit: This old name for an iron is a golf club.

clue.text: A note to finish a list of things to be seen to

definitions.text: list of things to be seen to

parts.note: G is a musical note
end means finish

explanation.surface: A memo tells someone to finish off their to-do list.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be handled at a meeting.

clue.text: The wig may give authority

indicators.note: the letters may give, rearranged, a new word

explanation.surface: A judge's wig may lend him authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Weight means influence or authority, as in someone whose opinion carries weight.

clue.text: The sovereign taken in by an alien assassin

indicators.note: the coin's letter is taken inside the word for alien

parts.note: a stranger is someone foreign, an alien
a sovereign was a pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A king is captured by a foreign killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sovereign' looks like a monarch, but it is a pound coin, giving L.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is a killer who throttles a victim.

clue.text: Annoyed about article, so got abusive

indicators.note: the word for annoyed goes around the article

parts.note: riled means irritated
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone irked by a newspaper piece became abusive.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain bitterly or abuse someone in words.

clue.text: Where children alone are cared for

definitions.text: Where children alone are cared for

parts.words: Where children alone are cared for
parts.note: reads like a place for kids left alone, but means a home for children with no parents

explanation.definitionFit: A home for children whose parents have died, who are thus left alone.

clue.text: He counts as an announcer

definitions.meaning: a bank clerk who counts cash, or one who counts votes
one who tells or relates something

explanation.definitionFit: A bank clerk counts money; and someone who tells a story or news is its narrator.

clue.text: The artificial language of peers-not a problem

indicators.note: the letters present a problem to be worked out, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lords claim it is easy to learn a made-up tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is the best-known constructed international language, devised by Zamenhof.
